Chosen: Incremental rollout — Extend live L5, add L4, defer L1-L3/L6 based on reuse evidence.

Iteration 1 -- ensure we have ENTIRELY ADDED QDRANT requirements and usability

Iteration 2 -- FULL Build out of the following all in parallel: 
- Code Graph
- File based memory (hive)
- Hive's sql and other levels of memory

Get to full 6 tiers at least and FULL INDEXING of files and such across the board

Next iteration, full metrics tracking and then eval, replace hive, or offer substitues and ways to test -- A/B test with full swarm and run metrics across and see
-- ensure we have all levels with expectations and integrations and even ways to turn off and then fallback to the levels or forward along (if someone only wants file based, fine, they all foward there and just realize that there is only one level available)

The integration of mnemosyne should know how many levels are available, what lives in each, and how to correctly find and index.  At this point Mnemosyne is truly v1 ready as it has the implementation in a way we can swap, we have our contracts defined, we have some level of swap out stubbed or replaceable, we have bits and pieces across the board to enable / disable and some UI to see all of the levels, the graphs, and the interactions (hell, if obsidian or another tool does all of this already, piggy back, but i don't think anythign does out of the box)
